body: Point `0, 0` is valid, so some other value should be used for invalid (line `MAX_INT, MAX_INT`).
When changing editor placement settings, floating window seems to apply it only on a second run, of sure exactly why.

I fixed an issue where the embedded game did not move with the floating window when placement changes and the game is running. Was it your issue? If not, can you give me more information? Are you on Windows or Linux, which version?

I was testing on Windows 11, the issue is still reproducible. 1. Set `Editor Settings -> Window Placement -> Screen` to `Screen 1` and run (works fine). 2. Set it to `Screen 2` and run (floating window appears in the middle of two screens). 3. Run it again, window is correctly placed on screen 2. So it seems to be an issue only if you change screen in between runs (first run after closing and reopening the editor is always correct). Screen config looks like this, both displays are set to 150% scale. Red box indicate incorrect placed floating window on step 2.

These 3 modes could have a string appended at the end to suggest the use of [feature tags](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/export/feature_tags.html) to override the window mode when running the project from the editor:

> Consider overriding the window mode project setting with the `editor` feature tag to Windowed to use game embedding while leaving the exported project intact.

Thanks for the information, very helpful. This issue should be fixed. The main reason was the third parameter of `window_wrapper->restore_window_from_saved_position`. When switching window, the screen rect was not valide anymore. I always pass an empty Rect to force the `restore_window_from_saved_position` method to recalculate.
Also, this method is bugged when passing negative screen index. When Primary screen was selected, -2 was passed causing index error. That's why I updated the `EditorRun::get_window_placement` method to always return a valid screen index.

Tested on Windows 11 and Linux Ubuntu.

I have added your suggested text to the messages. I also added some margin to the right and left sides to prevent the text from touching the edges.

I did not know we could do that in Godot!! Thanks!
